content.bodyUz:
**82 so'z**

*Hi Daniel,*

*Great news — you have picked the right country!*

*I'd avoid July if I were you: it gets brutally hot. Late April or September is far kinder, and the markets are full of fruit then.*

*As for the rest of the country, Samarkand is the obvious one, but do not skip Bukhara; it is smaller, quieter and, honestly, the one people remember. Two nights each is plenty.*

*Let me know your dates and I'll sort out the trains.*

*Take care,*
*Aziz*

Diqqat qiling: bu yerda bironta ham "katta" so'z yo'q. C1 ni ko'rsatayotgan narsa — **gap tuzilishining xilma-xilligi** va **so'zlarning bir-biriga tabiiy yopishishi**, lug'atdan olingan noyob so'zlar emas.

content.titleUz: Gap-bagap tahlil: har bir gap qanday ball keltirdi

items.en: Great news — you have picked the right country!
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH + ohang. Xat darrov do'stning xabariga reaksiya bilan boshlanadi, shablon bilan emas. Tire (—) norasmiy yozuvda tabiiy pauza yaratadi — C1 punktuatsiya belgisi. "Picked" (choose emas) — og'zaki registrga mos.

items.en: I'd avoid July if I were you: it gets brutally hot.
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA. Ikkinchi shart mayli (If I were you) qisqargan holda — maslahat buyruq emas, taklif bo'lib chiqadi. Ikki nuqta (:) sabab bog'lovchisi o'rnida ishlagan. "Brutally hot" — kuchli, tabiiy kollokatsiya; "very hot" bu yerda B1 bo'lardi.

items.en: Late April or September is far kinder, and the markets are full of fruit then.
items.uz: SO'Z BOYLIGI. "Kinder" ob-havo haqida ko'chma ma'noda — C1 belgisi. "Far + kinder" — kuchaytirgich (very emas). Ikkinchi qism savolga qo'shimcha sabab beradi: javob shunchaki fakt emas, **asoslangan** javob.

items.en: As for the rest of the country, Samarkand is the obvious one, but do not skip Bukhara; it is smaller, quieter and, honestly, the one people remember.
items.uz: IZCHILLIK. "As for..." — mavzuni ikkinchi savolga o'tkazuvchi signal (Secondly emas — bu tabiiyroq). "The obvious one" va "the one people remember" — takrorlashdan qochish uchun substitution. Nuqtali vergul ikki bog'liq fikrni ulaydi. "Honestly" — hedging: fikr shaxsiy ekanini yumshoq bildiradi.

items.en: Two nights each is plenty.
items.uz: RITM + VAZIFANI BAJARISH. Uzun gaplardan keyin qisqa gap — matnga nafas beradi va maslahatni aniq qiladi. "Each" bitta so'z bilan ikkala shaharga ham tegishli ekanini bildiradi — iqtisodiy ifoda.

items.en: Let me know your dates and I'll sort out the trains.
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH. Xat harakatga chaqirish bilan yakunlanadi — bu suhbatni davom ettiradi, ya'ni haqiqiy email vazifasini bajaradi. "Sort out" — norasmiy phrasal verb, registrga to'liq mos ("arrange" bu yerda biroz rasmiy bo'lardi).

items.en: Take care,
items.uz: REGISTR. Xayrlashuv salomlashish bilan bir xil darajada norasmiy. Agar "Hi Daniel" dan keyin "Yours faithfully" kelsa, register buziladi va ball tushadi — bu eng oson yo'qotiladigan ballardan biri.

rows: Vazifani bajarish
Ikkala savolga ham javob bor va har biri asoslangan; so'z chegarasi (82) ichida; javob suhbatni davom ettiradi.
Izchillik va bog'lanish
"As for..." bilan mavzu almashinuvi, substitution (the obvious one), nuqtali vergul va tire bilan tabiiy oqim. Bog'lovchilar sanoq shaklida emas.
So'z boyligi
brutally hot, far kinder, the one people remember, sort out — barchasi tabiiy kollokatsiya. Sun'iy "imtihon so'zlari" yo'q.
Grammatik xilma-xillik va aniqlik
Shart mayli, kelasi zamon (I'll), qiyoslash, sanoq sifatlar — xilma-xil va xatosiz. 5/5 uchun yana bitta murakkab struktura (masalan, relative clause) qo'shilishi mumkin edi.

content.bodyUz:
**147 so'z**

*Dear Dr Whitfield,*

*I am writing with regard to the two-week research placement in Environmental Science advertised on your department's website.*

*I am currently in my third year of a Chemistry degree at the National University of Uzbekistan, where my coursework has focused on water quality in the Aral basin. The placement appears to build directly on that work, which is why I am keen to be considered.*

*Before submitting an application, I would be grateful for clarification on two points. First, is accommodation arranged by the department, or are participants expected to make their own arrangements? Second, I understand that a limited number of bursaries are available; could you confirm whether international applicants are eligible?*

*I would also appreciate it if you could tell me what documents the application requires.*

*Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.*

*Yours sincerely,*
*Aziz Rahimov*

content.titleUz: Gap-bagap tahlil: har bir gap qanday ball keltirdi

items.en: I am writing with regard to the two-week research placement in Environmental Science advertised on your department's website.
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH. Birinchi gap uchta savolga bir yo'la javob beradi: kim yozyapti, nima haqida, qayerdan bilgan. "With regard to" — "about" ning rasmiy varianti. "Advertised on..." — qisqargan sifatdosh oborot (which was advertised o'rniga): iqtisodiy va rasmiy.

items.en: I am currently in my third year of a Chemistry degree at the National University of Uzbekistan, where my coursework has focused on water quality in the Aral basin.
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA + VAZIFA. "Where" bilan boshlangan relative clause ikkita fikrni bitta gapga jamlaydi. Present Perfect ("has focused") davom etayotgan tajribani bildiradi. Ma'lumot **tegishli** — vazifaga bog'liq, umumiy tarjimai hol emas.

items.en: The placement appears to build directly on that work, which is why I am keen to be considered.
items.uz: IZCHILLIK + HEDGING. "Appears to" — ehtiyotkor bahо ("is" deyish o'zini haddan tashqari ishonchli qilib ko'rsatardi). "Which is why" — oldingi butun gapga ishora qiluvchi bog'lovchi: bu C1 darajadagi izchillik quroli.

items.en: Before submitting an application, I would be grateful for clarification on two points.
items.uz: IZCHILLIK. Bu gap **signpost** — o'quvchini ogohlantiradi: hozir ikkita savol keladi. Ekspert bunday gaplarni juda qadrlaydi, chunki matn tuzilishi ko'rinib turadi. "Before + -ing" — qisqargan ergash gap.

items.en: First, is accommodation arranged by the department, or are participants expected to make their own arrangements?
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA. Ikkita majhul nisbat (passive) bitta savolda — rasmiy registrning tabiiy belgisi. Muqobil savol ("or") bitta so'rov bilan ikki variantni qamrab oladi: iqtisodiy va aniq.

items.en: Second, I understand that a limited number of bursaries are available; could you confirm whether international applicants are eligible?
items.uz: SO'Z BOYLIGI + ohang. "I understand that..." — ma'lumotni ehtiyotkorlik bilan tekshirish shakli; agar noto'g'ri bo'lsa ham, yozuvchi qo'pol ko'rinmaydi. "Could you confirm whether..." — bilvosita savol, "Are they eligible?" dan ancha hurmatliroq.

items.en: I would also appreciate it if you could tell me what documents the application requires.
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA. "I would appreciate it if you could..." — eng foydali rasmiy so'rov formulasi, ichida bilvosita savol ("what documents the application requires" — so'z tartibi to'g'ri, "what documents does..." emas). Bu yerda ko'p o'quvchi xato qiladi.

items.en: Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.
items.uz: REGISTR. Ikki qismli yakun: minnatdorchilik + kutish. "Look forward to" dan keyin -ing shakli (hearing) — klassik tuzoq, namunada to'g'ri. "Dear Dr Whitfield" ism ma'lum bo'lgani uchun "Yours sincerely" bilan yakunlangan.

rows: Vazifani bajarish
To'rt talabning barchasi bajarilgan, har biri alohida ajratilgan; ma'lumot vazifaga tegishli; 146 so'z — chegara ichida.
Izchillik va bog'lanish
"Before submitting..." signposti, First/Second sanoqlari, "which is why" bilan orqaga ishora — matn tuzilishi birinchi o'qishdayoq ko'rinadi.
So'z boyligi
with regard to, clarification, bursaries, eligible, make their own arrangements — aniq va sohaga mos. Takrorlanish yo'q.
Grammatik xilma-xillik va aniqlik
Relative clause, ikki passive, ikki bilvosita savol, qisqargan oborotlar, "I would appreciate it if..." — xilma-xil va xatosiz.
1. Maqsad
Nima haqida yozayotganingiz + manba
I am writing with regard to... advertised on your department's website.
2. Kontekst
Nega aynan siz — tegishli ma'lumot
I am currently in my third year..., where my coursework has focused on...
3. Signpost
Nechta savol borligini oldindan aytish
I would be grateful for clarification on two points.
4. Savollar
Bilvosita, ajratilgan, hurmatli
First, is accommodation arranged...? Second, could you confirm whether...?
5. Yakun
Minnatdorchilik + kutish + to'g'ri imzo
Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely,

content.bodyUz:
Rasmiy emailda **savol berish** ballning yarmini olib keladi. Uchta formulani yodlab qo'ying va imtihonda faqat ichini almashtiring:

1. *Could you confirm whether...?*
2. *I would be grateful if you could...*
3. *I would also appreciate it if you could tell me what/how/when...*

Muhim: ulardan keyin **to'g'ri gap tartibi** keladi — *what documents the application requires* (emas: *what documents does the application require*).

content.bodyUz:
**149 so'z**

*Dear Sir or Madam,*

*I am writing to complain about a guided tour I booked through your website on 12 May (booking reference UZ-4471).*

*According to the confirmation, an English-speaking guide was to meet our group at the Registan at 9 a.m. No one appeared. After forty minutes of phone calls, your office informed us that a replacement had been arranged; he eventually arrived at 11 a.m., without the promised transport.*

*As a result, we missed two of the four sites listed in the itinerary and had to cancel a museum booking made for the afternoon. For a tour advertised as "fully guided", this fell well short of what we were entitled to expect.*

*I would therefore ask you to refund half of the fee. If I do not receive a reply within ten working days, I will take the matter to the booking platform.*

*Yours faithfully,*
*Aziz Rahimov*

content.titleUz: Gap-bagap tahlil: har bir gap qanday ball keltirdi

items.en: I am writing to complain about a guided tour I booked through your website on 12 May (booking reference UZ-4471).
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH. Birinchi gapda maqsad, mahsulot, sana va bron raqami bor. Qavs ichidagi raqam — real hayotdagi shikoyatning belgisi; ekspert buni "vazifa kontekstini to'liq egallash" deb baholaydi. Relative clause "that" tushirilgan holda (a tour I booked) — tabiiy va iqtisodiy.

items.en: According to the confirmation, an English-speaking guide was to meet our group at the Registan at 9 a.m.
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA. "Was to meet" — kelishilgan, lekin bajarilmagan reja uchun ishlatiladigan struktura. Bu juda kuchli tanlov: shartnoma buzilganini grammatikaning o'zi aytib turibdi. "According to the confirmation" — dalilga havola.

items.en: No one appeared.
items.uz: USLUB. Uch so'zli gap uzun gapdan keyin — zarba effekti. C1 yozuvchi gap uzunligini **maqsadli** o'zgartiradi; bu izchillik va uslub nazoratining belgisi. Ohang qo'pol emas, lekin qat'iy.

items.en: After forty minutes of phone calls, your office informed us that a replacement had been arranged; he eventually arrived at 11 a.m., without the promised transport.
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA. Past Perfect Passive ("had been arranged") voqealar ketma-ketligini aniq ko'rsatadi. "Eventually" — kechikishga baho beruvchi ravish. Nuqtali vergul ikki bosqichni bitta voqea sifatida bog'laydi.

items.en: As a result, we missed two of the four sites listed in the itinerary and had to cancel a museum booking made for the afternoon.
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH — OQIBAT bosqichi. "As a result" bilan aniq bog'lanish. Raqamlar ("two of the four") zararni o'lchanadigan qiladi. Ikkita qisqargan sifatdosh oborot (listed..., made...) matnni ixcham saqlaydi.

items.en: For a tour advertised as "fully guided", this fell well short of what we were entitled to expect.
items.uz: SO'Z BOYLIGI. "Fall well short of" — kuchli idiomatik kollokatsiya; "be entitled to" huquqiy ohang qo'shadi. E'londagi so'zni qo'shtirnoqda keltirish — dalilni ularning o'z tili bilan qaytarish usuli. Baqirmasdan bosim o'tkazish shu.

items.en: I would therefore ask you to refund half of the fee.
items.uz: TALAB bosqichi. "I would therefore ask you to..." — qat'iy, lekin xushmuomala. "I want my money back" qo'pol, "Maybe you could refund something" esa kuchsiz bo'lardi. Talab **aniq va o'lchanadigan**: yarmi, hammasi emas — bu ishonchlilik qo'shadi.

items.en: If I do not receive a reply within ten working days, I will take the matter to the booking platform.
items.uz: GRAMMATIKA + strategiya. Birinchi shart mayli bilan keyingi qadam belgilanadi. Qisqartma yo'q (do not) — rasmiy registr saqlangan. Muddat aniq ("ten working days") — shikoyat kuchli bo'ladi.

rows: Vazifani bajarish
To'rt talab (bron / nosozlik / oqibat / talab) to'liq bajarilgan; detallar aniq va ishonarli; 148 so'z.
Izchillik va bog'lanish
Har xatboshi bir bosqich. "According to...", "As a result...", "therefore" — bog'lanish tabiiy, sanoq shaklida emas.
So'z boyligi
fall well short of, be entitled to, itinerary, replacement, refund — sohaga aniq mos. Kuchli ohang so'z tanlash orqali berilgan, undov belgilari orqali emas.
Grammatik xilma-xillik va aniqlik
was to meet, past perfect passive, qisqargan oborotlar, first conditional — xilma-xil va aniq. 5/5 uchun bitta murakkab qo'shma gap ko'proq bo'lishi mumkin edi.
I was a bit sad about the tour.
This fell well short of what we were entitled to expect.
Your company is a total disgrace.
Maybe you could give something back?
I would therefore ask you to refund half of the fee.
I demand my money back immediately!!!
Please answer when you can.
If I do not receive a reply within ten working days, I will take the matter to the booking platform.
Answer me now or I will destroy your reputation.

He eventually arrived at 11 a.m., without the promised transport.
The guide was completely useless and lazy.

content.bodyUz: Shikoyatda **undov belgisi ishlatmang**. C1 da kuchli ohang faktlar, raqamlar va aniq kollokatsiyalar orqali beriladi: *fell well short of*, *were entitled to*, *within ten working days*. Undov belgisi va bosh harflar (VERY BAD!) darhol registrni B1 ga tushiradi.

content.bodyUz:
Do'stingiz Mark yozdi:

> *I've been offered a job in another city. Better pay, but I'd be leaving all my friends. What would you do?*

Javob email yozing (**50-90 so'z**).

Quyida bir xil vazifaga yozilgan **uchta** javob bor. Ular bir xil g'oyani aytadi — "ishni qabul qil, lekin o'ylab ko'r". Farq **g'oyada emas, ifodada**. Ekspert ham aynan shuni baholaydi.

*Hi Mark,*

*Thanks for your email. It is a difficult question.*

*I think you should take the job. The money is better and you can find new friends there. Also you can visit your old friends at the weekend, because the city is not very far.*

*But it is your decision. Think about it carefully.*

*Good luck!*
*Aziz*

**Nega B1:** hamma gap bir xil uzunlikda va bir xil qurilishda (ega + kesim + to'ldiruvchi). Bog'lovchilar eng oddiylari: and, also, because, but. "It is a difficult question" — bo'sh gap, hech narsa qo'shmaydi. Maslahat berilgan, lekin **asoslanmagan**.

*Hi Mark,*

*What a decision to be faced with! I can see why you are hesitating.*

*If I were you, I would probably accept. A better salary now will give you more choice later, and friendships do not disappear the moment you move — you will just have to work a little harder at them.*

*That said, do ask how much travelling the job involves before you say yes.*

*Let me know what you decide!*
*Aziz*

**Nega B2, C1 emas:** struktura ancha yaxshi — shart mayli bor, "That said" bor, tire bor. Lekin ohang hali ham **maslahatchi** ohangi: "you should / do ask". Fikr aytilgan, lekin **qarshi tomon ko'rib chiqilmagan**. So'zlar to'g'ri, lekin kutilgan: better salary, more choice, work harder.

*Hi Mark,*

*Honestly? I'd take it.*

*Not because the money settles the argument — it rarely does — but because you can always move back, whereas an offer like this may not come round twice. Friendships survive distance far better than we expect; the ones that don't were probably on their way out anyway.*

*The one thing I would check is whether the role actually involves the work you enjoy, or just more of it.*

*Either way, you'll land on your feet.*
*Aziz*

**Nega C1:** javob birinchi qatorda beriladi, keyin **asoslanadi**; qarshi dalil ("not because the money...") ichkariga singdirilgan; gap uzunligi maqsadli o'zgaradi (2 so'z → 30 so'z → 5 so'z); ohang do'stona, lekin fikri bor odamning ohangi.

content.bodyUz:
> *Some people believe that governments should invest primarily in public transport, while others think that money is better spent on building new roads. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.*

**Talab:** 250-280 so'z, ~50 daqiqa.

**Eng ko'p uchraydigan xato:** o'quvchi ikkala fikrni bayon qiladi, lekin **o'z fikrini aytmaydi** yoki uni faqat oxirgi gapda eslatib o'tadi. Vazifada uchta talab bor: 1-fikr, 2-fikr, **va** o'z pozitsiyangiz. Uchtasidan biri yetishmasa, vazifani bajarish mezoni darhol tushadi.

**268 so'z**

*How a city spends its transport budget shapes daily life for decades, so the choice between expanding public transport and building new roads is far from technical. Both positions have a reasonable case, though I believe investment should favour public networks.*

*The argument for new roads rests on immediate relief. Congestion imposes real costs — hours lost, fuel wasted, emergency vehicles delayed — and additional lanes can ease pressure quickly, particularly on routes into industrial zones where goods, not commuters, are the priority. Supporters also point out that road building is politically straightforward: the results are visible within a single term of office.*

*The case for public transport is longer-term but, to my mind, more persuasive. Decades of evidence from cities such as Seoul and Bogotá suggest that new roads tend to fill up almost as soon as they open, a phenomenon known as induced demand. A metro line or a segregated bus corridor, by contrast, moves far more people per square metre of city and continues to do so as the population grows. There is also an equity dimension: not everyone can afford a car, and a transport policy built around private vehicles quietly excludes those who cannot.*

*That said, the two are not mutually exclusive, and the strongest systems combine them. My own view is that new road capacity should be justified case by case, whereas public transport deserves sustained, predictable funding rather than whatever remains at the end of the budget.*

*In conclusion, while roads answer today's congestion, public transport answers tomorrow's, and it is the second question that a serious transport policy has to get right.*

items.en: How a city spends its transport budget shapes daily life for decades, so the choice between expanding public transport and building new roads is far from technical.
items.uz: KIRISH. Diqqat qiling: "Nowadays transport is very important" yo'q. Gap **nominal ergash gap** bilan boshlanadi (How a city spends... = ega). "Far from technical" — mavzuni siyosiy/insoniy masala sifatida ramkalaydi. Bir gapda savol qayta ifodalangan va nega muhimligi ko'rsatilgan.

items.en: Both positions have a reasonable case, though I believe investment should favour public networks.
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH. Pozitsiya **kirishning oxirgi gapida** e'lon qilingan — ekspert uni birinchi 40 so'zdayoq topadi. "Though" bilan muvozanat: ikkala tomonni hurmat qilgan holda tanlov qilinadi. Bu "discuss both views" turining ideal kirishi.

items.en: Congestion imposes real costs — hours lost, fuel wasted, emergency vehicles delayed — and additional lanes can ease pressure quickly, particularly on routes into industrial zones where goods, not commuters, are the priority.
items.uz: SO'Z BOYLIGI + GRAMMATIKA. Tire ichidagi uchta qisqargan oborot (hours lost, fuel wasted, vehicles delayed) — parallel struktura, juda iqtisodiy. "Impose costs", "ease pressure" — aniq kollokatsiyalar. "Goods, not commuters" — qarama-qarshilikni ikki so'z bilan berish.

items.en: Supporters also point out that road building is politically straightforward: the results are visible within a single term of office.
items.uz: VAZIFANI BAJARISH. Qarshi tomonning dalili **adolatli va kuchli** qilib berilgan — bu C1 belgisi. Zaif o'quvchi qarshi fikrni ataylab kuchsiz ko'rsatadi. "Within a single term of office" — siyosiy kontekstga aniq mos ibora.

items.en: Decades of evidence from cities such as Seoul and Bogotá suggest that new roads tend to fill up almost as soon as they open, a phenomenon known as induced demand.
items.uz: DALIL + HEDGING. Aniq misollar (Seoul, Bogotá) dalilga og'irlik beradi. "Suggest" va "tend to" — ikki qatlamli hedging: yozuvchi "isbot" demaydi. "A phenomenon known as induced demand" — appozitsiya bilan atama kiritish: bilim ko'rsatiladi, lekin gapni cho'zmasdan.

items.en: A metro line or a segregated bus corridor, by contrast, moves far more people per square metre of city and continues to do so as the population grows.
items.uz: IZCHILLIK. "By contrast" gap o'rtasiga qo'yilgan — boshiga emas; bu ritmni tabiiy qiladi. "Continues to do so" — takrorlashdan qochish (do so = moves more people). "Per square metre of city" — mavhum dalilni o'lchanadigan qiladi.

items.en: There is also an equity dimension: not everyone can afford a car, and a transport policy built around private vehicles quietly excludes those who cannot.

items.en: My own view is that new road capacity should be justified case by case, whereas public transport deserves sustained, predictable funding rather than whatever remains at the end of the budget.
items.uz: POZITSIYA. Fikr **aniq va amaliy**: "men jamoat transportini yoqtiraman" emas, balki qanday siyosat kerakligi. "Whereas" bilan ikki yondashuv qarama-qarshi qo'yilgan. "Whatever remains at the end of the budget" — achchiq, esda qoladigan ifoda.

items.en: In conclusion, while roads answer today's congestion, public transport answers tomorrow's, and it is the second question that a serious transport policy has to get right.

content.bodyUz:
> *Some people think that university education should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?*

**Talab:** 250-280 so'z.

**"To what extent" nima degani:** savol sizdan **darajani** so'rayapti, ha/yo'q emas. Uch xil javob mumkin:

1. **To'liq roziman** — barcha xatboshilar bir tomonda;
2. **Umuman rozi emasman** — teskarisi;
3. **Asosan roziman, bitta shart bilan** — eng kuchli va eng tabiiy variant.

Namunada uchinchi yo'l tanlangan. U C1 uchun eng qulay, chunki qarshi dalilni ko'rib chiqishga imkon beradi va fikr yetuk ko'rinadi.

**261 so'z**

*The question of who should pay for a degree — the student or the taxpayer — resurfaces in almost every election. I largely agree that university education should be free at the point of use, though not without conditions.*

*The strongest argument is economic rather than sentimental. Graduates pay more tax over a lifetime, are less likely to claim benefits and staff the professions a country cannot function without. Seen this way, tuition fees are not a saving but a delay: the state either invests early or pays later for the shortage of teachers, engineers and doctors it failed to train. Countries such as Germany and Norway, which charge little or nothing, have not collapsed under the cost.*

*Fairness points in the same direction. Where fees are high, the decision to study is made not on ability but on how comfortable a family is with debt, and it is consistently the poorest students who decide the risk is not worth taking. Free tuition removes that filter.*

*Opponents object that free provision is regressive, since the taxpayer funds degrees for the wealthy as well. This has some force, but it is an argument for a progressive tax system, not for fees. A more serious concern is quality: unlimited free places can leave universities underfunded and overcrowded, which is why funding needs to be tied to standards.*

*On balance, then, I agree, with one qualification. Tuition should be free, but places should be allocated strictly on merit and institutions held to account for what they deliver. Free education that is not worth having helps nobody.*

content.bodyUz:
> *In many countries, young people are leaving rural areas to work in the capital. What problems does this cause, and what measures could be taken to address them?*

**Talab:** 250-280 so'z.

**Ushbu turdagi asosiy tuzoq — moslashmaslik.** O'quvchi 3 ta muammoni sanaydi, keyin 3 ta yechimni sanaydi, lekin ular bir-biriga bog'lanmaydi. Ekspert buni darhol ko'radi.

**Yechim:** kamroq nuqta, lekin har biri **chuqur**. Namunada 2 ta muammo maydoni (qishloq / poytaxt) va 3 ta yechim bor, ularning har biri aniq muammoga javob beradi.

**261 so'z**

*Every year, a further wave of young Uzbeks boards the train to Tashkent, and the villages they leave behind grow a little quieter. The trend is understandable, but it creates difficulties at both ends of the journey, and these can be reduced if the right measures are taken.*

*Rural areas suffer first. When those aged eighteen to thirty leave, the working population thins out, schools close for lack of pupils and small farms are left in the hands of people who can no longer manage them. What remains is a community that depends heavily on remittances and has little capacity to renew itself. The capital, meanwhile, absorbs more arrivals than its housing and transport were designed for, which pushes rents up and forces newcomers into insecure work.*

*The obvious response — restricting movement — would be neither fair nor effective. A more realistic approach is to reduce the reasons for leaving. Regional universities and vocational colleges should be funded to a standard that makes staying a genuine choice rather than a compromise, and tax incentives could be offered to firms that establish production outside the capital, as Turkey has done with some success.*

*Digital infrastructure deserves particular attention. Reliable high-speed internet allows programmers, designers and accountants to earn city salaries without moving, and it costs a fraction of what new urban housing does.*

*None of this will reverse migration entirely, nor should it: mobility is a sign of a functioning economy. The aim should be to ensure that young people move because they want to, not because their home region offers them nothing.*

content.bodyUz:
> *An increasing number of companies allow their employees to work entirely from home. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?*

**Talab:** 250-280 so'z.

**Savolni diqqat bilan o'qing:** "Do the advantages **outweigh** the disadvantages?" — bu **tarozi** savoli. Faqat ro'yxat berish yetarli emas; siz **qaysi tomon og'irroq** ekanini aytishingiz kerak.

Eng kuchli C1 javobi ko'pincha **shartli** bo'ladi: "ha, og'irroq — **lekin faqat agar** ...". Bu esseni oddiy "plus/minus" ro'yxatidan chiqaradi.

**263 so'z**

*A decade ago, working from home was a concession granted to a handful of employees; today whole companies operate without an office at all. The shift brings clear gains, but they are unevenly distributed, and on balance I would say the advantages outweigh the drawbacks only where the arrangement is managed deliberately.*

*The benefits to the individual are easy to state. A commute of an hour each way returns roughly ten hours a week to the person who no longer makes it, and that time tends to go to family, sleep or study. Employers benefit too: office space is expensive, and recruiting without a fifty-kilometre radius opens up a far wider pool of candidates. For parents, and for people with disabilities in particular, remote work can be the difference between employment and none.*

*The costs, however, are subtler and take longer to appear. Junior staff learn a great deal by overhearing experienced colleagues, and that informal training largely disappears on video calls. Teams that never meet tend to lose the loose social ties that make difficult conversations possible. There is also the boundary problem: when the desk is in the bedroom, the working day quietly expands, and the hours saved on commuting are absorbed by the job.*

*Much depends, then, on implementation. Companies that keep occasional in-person meetings, protect people's evenings and invest in structured mentoring capture most of the benefit and avoid the worst of the harm.*

*Overall, I believe the advantages do outweigh the disadvantages, but only for organisations willing to rebuild deliberately what an office used to provide by accident.*

items.en: A decade ago, working from home was a concession granted to a handful of employees; today whole companies operate without an office at all.
items.uz: KIRISH. "Nowadays" o'rniga **vaqt qarama-qarshiligi**: o'n yil oldin ↔ bugun. Nuqtali vergul ikki davrni bitta gapda taqqoslaydi. "A concession granted to a handful" — aniq va tejamkor (qisqargan sifatdosh oborot).

items.en: The shift brings clear gains, but they are unevenly distributed, and on balance I would say the advantages outweigh the drawbacks only where the arrangement is managed deliberately.
items.uz: POZITSIYA. Savolning fe'li ("outweigh") to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ishlatilgan — ekspert javobni aniq ko'radi. "Only where..." — shart darhol qo'yiladi, ya'ni esse oddiy plus/minus emas. "Unevenly distributed" — nozik fikr: foyda bor, lekin hammaga emas.

items.en: A commute of an hour each way returns roughly ten hours a week to the person who no longer makes it, and that time tends to go to family, sleep or study.
items.uz: AFZALLIK — O'LCHANGAN. Mavhum "vaqt tejaladi" o'rniga **hisob**: 10 soat. "Roughly" hedgingi aniqlikni haddan tashqari qat'iy qilib qo'ymaydi. Ikkinchi qism vaqt qayerga ketishini ko'rsatadi — dalil to'liq bo'ladi.

items.en: Employers benefit too: office space is expensive, and recruiting without a fifty-kilometre radius opens up a far wider pool of candidates.
items.uz: PERSPEKTIVA ALMASHUVI. Ikki nuqta bilan tushuntirish. Yozuvchi bir tomondan (xodim) ikkinchi tomonga (ish beruvchi) o'tadi — bu esseni ko'p qirrali qiladi. "A far wider pool of candidates" — aniq HR kollokatsiyasi.

items.en: For parents, and for people with disabilities in particular, remote work can be the difference between employment and none.
items.uz: FIKR CHUQURLIGI. Adolat o'lchami kiritiladi. "The difference between employment and none" — ellipsis (none = no employment) va kuchli, esda qoladigan ifoda. "In particular" urg'uni to'g'ri joyga qo'yadi.

items.en: The costs, however, are subtler and take longer to appear.
items.uz: O'TISH. "However" gap o'rtasida — vergullar bilan ajratilgan; bu tabiiyroq ko'rinadi. "Subtler" — kamchiliklar nima uchun ko'rinmasligini bir so'z bilan tushuntiradi va keyingi gaplarni tayyorlaydi.

items.en: Junior staff learn a great deal by overhearing experienced colleagues, and that informal training largely disappears on video calls.
items.uz: KAMCHILIK — ORIGINAL. Bu standart "lonely at home" dalili emas. "Overhearing" — aniq va kutilmagan fe'l. "That informal training" — oldingi fikrni ot bilan umumlashtirish (nominalizatsiya): kuchli izchillik quroli.

items.en: There is also the boundary problem: when the desk is in the bedroom, the working day quietly expands, and the hours saved on commuting are absorbed by the job.
items.uz: HALQA. Bu gap 2-xatboshidagi "ten hours a week" ga qaytadi va uni bekor qiladi — dalil bilan qarshi dalil bir-biriga ulanadi. "Quietly expands" va "are absorbed by" — ikkita nozik, aniq ifoda.

items.en: Companies that keep occasional in-person meetings, protect people's evenings and invest in structured mentoring capture most of the benefit and avoid the worst of the harm.
items.uz: SHARTNI OCHISH. Uchta parallel fe'l (keep / protect / invest) bitta relative clause ichida. Gap uzun, lekin tuzilishi shaffof. Bu "only where it is managed deliberately" shartining **amaliy mazmuni**.

items.en: Overall, I believe the advantages do outweigh the disadvantages, but only for organisations willing to rebuild deliberately what an office used to provide by accident.
items.uz: XULOSA. Ta'kidlovchi "do" (do outweigh) — grammatik urg'u. Oxirgi ibora ("rebuild deliberately what an office used to provide by accident") — butun essening g'oyasini bitta antitezaga siqadi. Aynan shunday yakunlar 70/75 keltiradi.

content.titleUz: To'rt mezon nimani o'lchaydi (va nimani o'lchamaydi)
content.bodyUz:
**1. Vazifani bajarish** — savolga to'liq javob berdingizmi, pozitsiya aniqmi, dalillar rivojlantirilganmi, so'z chegarasi hurmat qilinganmi.
*O'lchamaydi:* fikringiz "to'g'ri" yoki "noto'g'ri" ekanini. Ekspert siz bilan rozi bo'lishi shart emas.

**2. Izchillik va bog'lanish** — xatboshilar mantiqiy joylashganmi, o'tishlar tabiiymi, takrorlash substitution/ellipsis bilan yo'q qilinganmi.
*O'lchamaydi:* bog'lovchilar **sonini**. 10 ta "Firstly/Moreover/Furthermore" balni ko'tarmaydi, aksincha tushiradi.

**3. So'z boyligi** — so'zlar aniqmi, kollokatsiyalar tabiiymi, registr bir xilmi, takror yo'qmi.
*O'lchamaydi:* so'zlarning "qiyinligini". Noto'g'ri ishlatilgan noyob so'z — bu minus, plus emas.

**4. Grammatik xilma-xillik va aniqlik** — turli strukturalar bormi va ular xatosizmi.
*O'lchamaydi:* faqat xatolarni. Xatosiz, lekin bir xil oddiy gaplardan iborat matn ham yuqori ball olmaydi.

content.bodyUz:
> *Some people think that all museums should be free of charge. To what extent do you agree?*

**Javob (242 so'z):**

*Nowadays, museums are very important for every society. Some people think that all museums should be free of charge, but other people don't agree with this opinion. In this essay I will discuss this topic and give my opinion.*

*Firstly, museums are free is good because everybody can visit them. If a family has not much money, they can't pay expensive tickets, so their children will never see the history of their country. This is not fair. Secondly, free museums attract more tourists and tourists spend money in restaurants and hotels, so the country gets benefit anyway.*

*On the other hand, museums need money for salaries, electricity and repairing of old buildings. If there is no ticket, the government must pay everything, and maybe the government will reduce the budget for other important things like hospitals. In addition, when something is free, some people don't respect it and museums become very crowded.*

*In addition, I think there is a middle way. Museums can be free for students, pensioners and children, and other visitors can pay a small price. Also there can be one free day in a week for everybody. This system works in many European countries and it is very effective.*

*In conclusion, I agree that museums should be free but not for everybody and not always. Governments must support museums with the budget, and museums must find sponsors also. In my opinion, this is the best solution for this problem.*

content.titleUz: Baholash bosqichlari (avval o'zingiz, keyin javobni oching)
content.bodyUz:
Har bir mezon uchun **B1 / B2 / C1** dan birini tanlang va **bitta dalil** yozing — matndan aniq iqtibos bilan.

1. **Vazifani bajarish:** savolga javob berilganmi? Pozitsiya qayerda? "To what extent" darajasi ko'rsatilganmi?
2. **Izchillik:** bog'lovchilar to'g'ri ishlatilganmi? Bir xil bog'lovchi takrorlanmayaptimi?
3. **So'z boyligi:** takrorlanuvchi so'zlarni sanang. Nechta aniq kollokatsiya bor?
4. **Grammatika:** nechta xil struktura bor? Nechta xato topdingiz?

Baho yozib bo'lgach, quyidagi jadval bilan solishtiring. Farq katta bo'lsa — bu yaxshi: aynan shu farq sizning "ko'zingiz" qayerda sozlanmaganini ko'rsatadi.

rows: Vazifani bajarish

Savolga javob bor va pozitsiya oxirida aniqlanadi, lekin kirishda "In this essay I will discuss" dan boshqa hech narsa yo'q. "To what extent" darajasi faqat xulosada paydo bo'ladi. 4-xatboshidagi "middle way" — yaxshi g'oya, lekin u yerda emas, kirishda turishi kerak edi.
Izchillik va bog'lanish
"In addition" ketma-ket ikki marta, ikkinchisi noto'g'ri ma'noda (qo'shimcha emas, qarama-qarshilik/burilish kerak edi). Firstly/Secondly mexanik. Xatboshilar orasida haqiqiy o'tish yo'q.
So'z boyligi

Umumiy so'zlar ustun: important, good, money, things, problem. "Gets benefit", "a small price", "repairing of old buildings" — noto'g'ri kollokatsiyalar. Aniq atama deyarli yo'q (subsidy, admission fee, endowment kabi).
Grammatik xilma-xillik va aniqlik
"Museums are free is good" — jiddiy tuzilish xatosi. Qisqartmalar (don't, can't) akademik esseda o'rinsiz. Deyarli barcha gaplar Present Simple va bir xil qurilishda. Bitta shart mayli ham yo'q.
Umumiy
≈ B2 boshi (55/75 atrofida)
G'oyalar bor va tushunarli, lekin ifoda darajasi ularni ko'tarmayapti. Eng tez ko'tariladigan mezon — grammatik xilma-xillik.

items.en: Nowadays, museums are very important for every society.
items.uz: BO'SH OCHILISH. Hech qanday ma'lumot yo'q va mavzuga xos emas — bu gapni istalgan esseda ishlatish mumkin. C1 varianti: aniq qarama-qarshilik yoki raqam bilan boshlash. 8 so'z behuda ketdi.

items.en: In this essay I will discuss this topic and give my opinion.
items.uz: META-GAP. Ekspert nima qilishingizni biladi — aytish shart emas. Bu gap o'rniga **pozitsiyangizni** yozing. Vazifani bajarish mezoniga hech narsa qo'shmaydi, faqat so'z chegarasini yeydi.

items.en: Firstly, museums are free is good because everybody can visit them.
items.uz: GRAMMATIK XATO. Ikkita gap bir-biriga urilgan. To'g'risi: *Making museums free is a good idea because...* yoki *Free admission is desirable because...*. Bu turdagi xato grammatika balini darhol B1 ga tushiradi.

items.en: so the country gets benefit anyway
items.uz: KOLLOKATSIYA XATOSI. "Get benefit" ingliz tilida yo'q. To'g'risi: *benefits either way* yoki *the country gains regardless*. "Anyway" ham bu yerda og'zaki registr — akademik esseda "regardless" yoki "either way" kerak.

items.en: In addition, I think there is a middle way.
items.uz: NOTO'G'RI BOG'LOVCHI. Oldingi xatboshi ham "In addition" bilan tugagan edi, endi bu xatboshi ham shu bilan boshlanyapti — takror. Bundan tashqari, bu yerda qo'shimcha emas, **burilish** bo'lyapti: *There is, however, a middle way.* kerak edi.

items.en: This system works in many European countries and it is very effective.
items.uz: ASOSSIZ DA'VO. Qaysi mamlakatlar? Qanday ishlaydi? "Very effective" — o'lchanmagan. C1 varianti: *The Louvre, for instance, admits under-26s from the EU free of charge and still covers most of its costs.* Aniqlik dalilni kuchaytiradi.

items.en: In my opinion, this is the best solution for this problem.
items.uz: BO'SH YAKUN. Yangi ma'lumot yo'q, oldingi gapni takrorlaydi. "This... this..." ko'rsatkichlari noaniq. Oxirgi gap — umumiy taassurot shakllanadigan joy; uni behuda sarflash kechirilmas yo'qotish.

content.bodyUz: Baholashni **doim mezon bo'yicha alohida** qiling, umumiy taassurot bilan emas. Ko'p o'quvchi "yaxshi yozilgan" deb umumiy baho beradi va nima qilish kerakligini bilmay qoladi. Mezon bo'yicha ajratsangiz, javob aniq bo'ladi: bu esseda eng past mezon — grammatik xilma-xillik, demak **birinchi navbatda shu ustida ishlash kerak**.

content.bodyUz:
**Mikro-o'zgarish** — bu bir gapni qayta yozmasdan, uning **tuzilishini yoki aniqligini** kuchaytiruvchi kichik tahrir. U 10-30 soniya oladi, lekin mezonga bevosita ta'sir qiladi.

**Bu mikro-o'zgarish EMAS:**
- *important* → *paramount* (shunchaki katta so'z; ko'pincha noto'g'ri chiqadi)
- *very good* → *extremely good* (kuchaytirgichni almashtirish hech narsa bermaydi)
- gapga yana bitta "Furthermore" qo'shish

**Bu mikro-o'zgarish:**
- egani o'zgartirish (*People think that...* → *It is widely thought that...*)
- ikki gapni bittaga bog'lash (*This is a problem. It affects families.* → *This is a problem which affects families most directly.*)
- mavhum so'zni o'lchanadigan qilish (*a lot of money* → *roughly a third of the budget*)

> In many countries, people are living and working longer, and some governments have raised the official retirement age. What problems does this create, and what could be done to address them?

data.statement: Yozib bo'lgach darhol tekshirgan ma'qul — vaqt o'tsa, xatolarni yomonroq ko'rasiz.

exercises.promptEn: TASK 1 (120-150 words). You recently attended a two-day professional training course organised by your employer. The course was cancelled halfway through the second day without explanation, and the promised certificate has not arrived. Write an email to the training provider: give the details of the course, explain what went wrong, describe how this affected you, and state what you expect them to do. Use formal register throughout, at least two indirect questions or polite requests, and no exclamation marks.
exercises.promptUz: TASK 1 (120-150 so'z). Yaqinda ish beruvchingiz tashkil qilgan ikki kunlik kasbiy kursda qatnashdingiz. Kurs ikkinchi kunning yarmida sababsiz bekor qilindi va va'da qilingan sertifikat ham kelmadi. O'quv markaziga email yozing: kurs tafsilotlarini bering, nima noto'g'ri ketganini tushuntiring, bu sizga qanday ta'sir qilganini ayting va nima kutayotganingizni bildiring. Boshdan oxir rasmiy registr, kamida ikkita bilvosita savol yoki xushmuomala so'rov, undov belgisiz.

exercises.promptEn: TASK 2 (250-280 words). In many countries, people are living and working longer, and some governments have raised the official retirement age. What problems does this create, and what could be done to address them? Plan first: state your framing in the introduction, match each measure to a specific problem, vary your modal verbs (should / could / needs to), and include at least three different complex structures.
exercises.promptUz: TASK 2 (250-280 so'z). Ko'p mamlakatlarda odamlar uzoqroq yashab, uzoqroq ishlamoqda va ba'zi hukumatlar rasmiy nafaqa yoshini oshirdi. Bu qanday muammolar keltirib chiqaradi va ularni hal qilish uchun nima qilish mumkin? Avval reja tuzing: kirishda masalani ramkalang, har bir chorani aniq muammoga moslang, modal fe'llarni o'zgartiring (should / could / needs to) va kamida uchta har xil murakkab struktura ishlating.
